correctness.rationale: Direct geodesic-to-quotient-tree equivalence; the quotient must be a star for at least two selected edges, giving a unique connected core and bijection with its edge boundary. At one edge, both sides of a tree edge give a double count, establishing the exact subtraction. The rooted child inclusion/exclusion gives an inductive connected-boundary recurrence. The maximum multiplicity follows from an injective association of complement components with original leaves and independent choices of one cut on every terminal arm. Exhaustive and sampled independently constructed geodesics tested 1,429,023 subsets of 19,254 trees, and separate boundary/extremal tests passed; finite tests supplement rather than prove the general statement.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The literature results bound or determine a single maximum size; such scalar results cannot determine all polynomial coefficients or the count of maximum sets. The 2024 general-position polynomial uses vertex sets, so it neither specializes to nor dominates the edge enumeration.

originality.rationale: The 2021 foundation proves only the tree edge-general-position maximum, not the polynomial or extremal multiplicities; 2022/2023 adjacent full texts address scalar generalized/extremal parameters. A 2024 vertex-set polynomial counts distinct objects. The explicit connected-boundary bijection for all edge-position sets and terminal-arm maximum multiplicity were not found in compared sources or the specified indexed searches. Prior connected-subtree boundary-counting methods can calculate the auxiliary polynomial but do not, in the inspected material, identify it with the edge-general-position polynomial. Unindexed equivalent formulations remain possible.
residual_risks: A connected-subtree boundary enumerator may already be known and an unindexed publication may have explicitly identified it with tree edge-general-position sets.

Some broad combinatorial polynomial references, including historical connected-subtree boundary literature, were not exhaustively inspected in full; no originality conclusion relies on claiming those older techniques new.

value.rationale: The theorem counts every possible cardinality of a motivated edge-position invariant for arbitrary trees and forests, gives a uniform recursive computation, and upgrades the literature scalar leaf maximum to an exact multiplicity depending on all terminal arm lengths. These are structural and global enumerative results for a natural family; the known scalar result and the auxiliary connected-boundary counting technology are explicitly not misclaimed.
